title: Scala compile failures
hypothesis: At least 70% of seeded code faults are repaired within 3 attempts; repeated fingerprints escalate; forbidden APIs never run.
conclusion: 15 of 20 seeded faults were detected before execution. Forbidden APIs: 5 of 5 refused by gate 2, the static scan, so none was compiled let alone submitted - the PRD's strongest claim, and it holds. Per class: type_mismatch 5/5 detected at gate(s) [4]; missing_import 5/5 detected at gate(s) [4]; wrong_column 0/5 detected at gate(s) [None]; forbidden_api 5/5 detected at gate(s) [2]. Fingerprints repeat identically across three attempts: True, so an unrepairable fault trips the circuit breaker rather than burning the attempt budget. The expected observation about semantic faults holds in a stronger form than the PRD states it: a wrong column name does not merely escalate more often, it passes every static gate, because the name is a string until Spark resolves it. Repair rate is not measured - see the limitations.
limitations: Repair rate is not measured. Rewriting a generated slot requires an LLM provider and none is configured (ADR-0003); `StageRunner._apply_fix` adjusts infrastructure inputs only, so `generate` returns identical code on every attempt. A measured 0% would describe the missing provider, not the repair loop, so it is recorded as not measured rather than reported as a number.

`reached_execution` means the gates passed and a real run would have submitted the job. The Spark submission itself is not performed for the 5 wrong_column faults, so what gate 6/7/9 would report about each of them is not measured here.
